'''James Drewry Stewart''', {{Post-nominals|country=CAN|MSC}} (March 29, 1941{{spaced ndash}}December 3, 2014) was a Canadian mathematician, violinist, and [[professor emeritus]] of mathematics at [[McMaster University]]. Stewart is best known for his series of [[calculus]] textbooks used for high school, college, and university-level courses.

==Career==
Stewart received his Master of Science at [[Stanford University]] and his doctor of philosophy from the [[University of Toronto]] in 1967. He worked for two years as a postdoctoral fellow at the [[University of London]], where his research focused on [[harmonic analysis|harmonic]] and [[functional analysis]]. His books are standard textbooks in universities in many countries. One of his best-known textbooks is ''Calculus: Early Transcendentals'' (1995),<ref>{{Cite book | url=https://books.google.com/books?id=wsTbft6GDtcC |title = Single Variable Essential Calculus: Early Transcendentals|isbn = 978-1-133-11278-5|last1 = Stewart|first1 = James|date = 2012-01-06| publisher=Cengage Learning }}</ref> a set of textbooks which is accompanied by a [http://stewartcalculus.com website] for students.

Stewart was also a violinist and a former member of the [[Hamilton Philharmonic Orchestra]].<ref name="xtra" />

== Integral House ==
{{Main|Integral House}}

From 2003 to 2009<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/science/alexs-adventures-in-numberland/2015/oct/05/maths-palace-built-by-calculus-rock-star-on-sale-for-14m|title=Maths palace built by calculus 'rock star' on sale for £11.4m|last=Bellos|first=Alex|date=2015-10-05|work=The Guardian|access-date=2019-02-28|language=en-GB|issn=0261-3077}}</ref> a house designed by [[Brigitte Shim]] and Howard Sutcliffe was constructed for Stewart in the Rosedale neighbourhood of Toronto at a cost of $32 million. He paid an additional $5.4 million for the existing house and lot which was torn down to make room for his new home.<ref>[https://www.thestar.com/news/article/933017--the-house-that-math-built "The House that Math Built".] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121023121105/http://www.thestar.com/news/article/933017--the-house-that-math-built |date=2012-10-23 }} [[TheStar.com]]. 2011-02-04</ref> Called [[Integral House]] (a reference to its curved walls, and their similarity to the mathematical [[integral symbol]]), the house includes a concert hall that seats 150. Stewart has said, "My books and my house are my twin legacies. If I hadn't commissioned the house I'm not sure what I would have spent the money on." [[Glenn Lowry]], director of the [[Museum of Modern Art]], called the house "one of the most important private houses built in North America in a long time."<ref>[https://www.wsj.com/articles/SB123872378357585295 "An 'Accordion' of Wood and Glass"] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170820051758/https://www.wsj.com/articles/SB123872378357585295 |date=2017-08-20 }}, ''[[Wall Street Journal]]'', 2009-04-03; retrieved 2009-04-08.</ref>

== Personal life and political activism ==
Stewart was gay and involved in [[LGBT]] activism. According to [[Joseph Clement (filmmaker)|Joseph Clement]], a documentary filmmaker who is working on a film about Stewart and Integral House, Stewart brought gay rights activist [[George Hislop]] to speak at [[McMaster University|McMaster]] in the early 1970s, when the LGBT liberation movement was in its infancy, and was involved in protests and demonstrations.<ref name="xtra">{{cite news |url=http://dailyxtra.com/toronto/life/proud-lives/the-many-parts-james-stewart-96867 |title=The many parts of James Stewart |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141213232150/http://dailyxtra.com/toronto/life/proud-lives/the-many-parts-james-stewart-96867 |archive-date=December 13, 2014 |publisher=The Daily Xtra}}</ref>

== Death ==
In the summer of 2013, Stewart was diagnosed with [[multiple myeloma]], a blood cancer.<ref>[https://www.theglobeandmail.com/news/national/for-millionaire-mathematician-james-stewart-music-will-play-on-after-his-death/article20714879 "For millionaire mathematician James Stewart, music will play on after his death"] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170501124833/http://www.theglobeandmail.com/news/national/for-millionaire-mathematician-james-stewart-music-will-play-on-after-his-death/article20714879/|date=2017-05-01}}, ''[[The Globe and Mail]]'', 2014-09-21.</ref> He died on December 3, 2014, aged 73.<ref>[http://www.fields.utoronto.ca/press/14-15/JimStewart2014.html Press Release] {{webarchive|url=https://archive.today/20141204165059/http://www.fields.utoronto.ca/press/14-15/JimStewart2014.html|date=2014-12-04}}, fields.utoronto.ca, 2014-12-04.</ref>

==Honors==
In 2015, he was posthumously awarded the [[Meritorious Service Cross]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.gg.ca/en/honours/recipients/136-10112|title=Meritorious Service Cross Citation}}</ref>
